title: Candidate laboratory partners for fs-written waveguides in silica (project Silice-Neuro3D-Cube)
constraints_respected: Public information only. Nobody was contacted, no form was submitted, no message was sent. No personal email addresses or phone numbers were collected; only institutional or company pages.

fit_rubric.5: Documents fs-writing in silica or borosilicate near 1550 nm AND trench/depressed-cladding or equivalent AND a stated route for external users AND cut-back/near-field metrology AND no major barrier. No candidate reached 5.
fit_rubric.4: Strong documented capability for most of the ask plus either a stated external-user/contract route or an obvious academic fit; at most one important gap.
fit_rubric.3: Relevant capability but a material gap: other glass or wavelength, no stated external route, or unclear whether the group fabricates in-house.
fit_rubric.2: Weak or indirect evidence, the official page does not state the capability, or a significant practical barrier.

repository_licence_check.finding: The public repository's default branch has no LICENSE file: the GitHub API returns license = null and /contents/LICENSE on main gives 404. An Apache-2.0 LICENSE exists on the branch agent/scientific-closure-20261012, which is 3 commits ahead of main (compare API, 2026-10-13). Docs/CIERRE-20261012/T28-FABRICATION-DOSSIER.md exists on both branches.
repository_licence_check.action_for_owner: Merge the licence commit to main (or point partners to the branch) before sending any email; otherwise 'open code' cannot be reused legally by the partner.

candidates.name: Grupo de Investigación en Aplicaciones del Láser y Fotónica (ALF-USAL)
candidates.institution: Universidad de Salamanca (recognised research group; consolidated research unit UIC016)
leads_public: Carolina Romero and Javier Rodríguez Vázquez de Aldana (authors of the cited papers)
Luis Plaja Rustein (group leader per the Junta de Castilla y León science portal; the group's own site does not name a leader, so check)
candidates.why_fit: Most Spanish fs-writing output in the OpenAlex search of 2026-10-13 (44 works since 2019 for 'femtosecond laser written waveguide' with a USAL author). Official site lists the research line 'Device manufacturing for integrated photonics', two Ti:sapphire CPA systems (800 nm; 1 kHz/120 fs and, since 2019, 5 kHz/60 fs) and a 3-axis workstation 'for manufacturing photonic devices and precision microprocessing' (its laser parameters are not stated). Verified glass work: 2D and 3D Y-splitters and single-mode guides in Er/Yb oxyfluoride nano-glass ceramics (1.6 dB/cm, visible/NIR). Depressed-cladding writing is documented, in crystals (tapered circular cladding in Nd:YAG).

evidence.shows: fs inscription of 2D/3D Y-splitters in Er/Yb nano-glass ceramics; 1.6 dB/cm; abstract read.
evidence.crossref_title: Femtosecond laser direct inscription of 3D photonic devices in Er/Yb-doped oxyfluoride nano-glass ceramics

evidence.cite: Romero, García Ajates, Vázquez de Aldana
evidence.shows: tapered circular depressed-cladding waveguides in Nd:YAG (crystal); title and authors only.

evidence.crossref_title: Tapered depressed-cladding waveguide lasers modulated by Ag nanoparticles embedded in SiO2

evidence.cite: Bonduelle, ..., Vázquez de Aldana, Arroyo Heras, Romero
evidence.shows: all-DLW building blocks at 3.39-4.1 um (ALF-USAL affiliation confirmed in Crossref); not 1550 nm.
evidence.crossref_title: A route to an all direct laser written integrated FTS (SWIFTS) in the 3.39–4.1 μm range

collaboration_mode: R&D contract (services under a research contract, per its collaborations page)
candidates.barrier: Its collaborations page says it collaborates with other groups 'only with those with joined publications or patents' and serves companies and institutions under research contracts, so a first contact from an independent researcher may be routed to a paid contract. No low-loss silica or borosilicate recipe at 1550 nm and no cut-back set-up are documented on the site (listed instruments: spectrometers, M2, beam profiler, LIBS). Sources are 1-5 kHz class, not the high-repetition-rate regime of the best published silica results.
candidates.barrier_short: Collaborates 'only with those with joined publications or patents'; outside parties are served under paid research contracts; no 1550 nm silica data.
candidates.fit_reason: Spanish, documented depressed-cladding experience and a stated contract route; silica/borosilicate loss at 1550 nm is not yet shown by them.
not_verified: whether workstation 2 can write fused silica or borosilicate at 1550 nm quality

Value read in the open full text by the T26 second reader; the Crossref abstract says 'below 0.1 dB/cm'.

en.text:
Subject: Request for a small pilot: fs-written trench waveguides in silica, cut-back at 1550 nm

Dear [Prof./Dr. Name],

I am Francisco Angulo de Lafuente, an independent researcher in Spain. I am looking for a laboratory to run one physical test for an open study of femtosecond-laser-written optical networks in glass.

Already public: a preregistered numerical study; four registered tests designed to refute its own claims (one withdrew an energy-advantage claim); a verified literature review; registered predictions of the 1550 nm loss of trench (depressed-cladding) guides, fixed before any measurement; and a fabrication dossier.

The request: a pilot run of about three chips with straight trench guides at four lengths (1-4 cm), written in the glass and with the laser recipe you judge best, plus a cut-back measurement at 1550 nm. Optionally, a coupon of waveguide crossings in series. I do not prescribe writing parameters.

In return: co-authorship under CRediT roles agreed beforehand, open raw data and code, and a registered prediction that your data can confirm or refute. Negative results are published on the same terms.

Repository and dossier: https://github.com/Agnuxo1/Silice-Neuro3D-Cube (Docs/CIERRE-20261012/T28-FABRICATION-DOSSIER.md)

If this fits your group, or you know who it would fit, I would be grateful for a short reply.

Kind regards,
Francisco Angulo de Lafuente

es.text:
Asunto: Propuesta de un piloto: guías de trinchera escritas con láser de femtosegundo en sílice, medida cut-back a 1550 nm

Estimado/a [Prof./Dr./Dra. Nombre]:

Soy Francisco Angulo de Lafuente, investigador independiente en España. Busco un laboratorio que haga una prueba física para un estudio abierto sobre redes ópticas escritas con láser de femtosegundo en vidrio.

Ya es público: un estudio numérico prerregistrado; cuatro pruebas registradas para refutar sus propias afirmaciones (una retiró una ventaja energética); una revisión bibliográfica verificada; predicciones registradas de la pérdida a 1550 nm de guías de trinchera (revestimiento deprimido), fijadas antes de medir; y un dossier de fabricación.

Lo que pido: un piloto de unos tres chips con guías de trinchera rectas en cuatro longitudes (1-4 cm), escritas en el vidrio y con la receta que ustedes consideren mejor, y una medida de cut-back a 1550 nm. Opcionalmente, un cupón de cruces de guías en serie. No impongo parámetros de escritura.

A cambio: coautoría (roles CRediT acordados antes), datos en bruto y código abiertos, y una predicción registrada que sus datos pueden confirmar o refutar. Los resultados negativos se publican en las mismas condiciones.

Repositorio y dossier: https://github.com/Agnuxo1/Silice-Neuro3D-Cube (Docs/CIERRE-20261012/T28-FABRICATION-DOSSIER.md)

Si encaja con su grupo, o sabe a quién, le agradecería una breve respuesta.

Un saludo cordial,
Francisco Angulo de Lafuente
